react_result.final_narrative_text: Multi-paradigm pathway analysis of seven differentially abundant metabolites identified Galactose Metabolism as the overwhelmingly dominant affected pathway across three independent methods: RaMP multi-DB ORA returned FDR = 2.83e-11 (rank 1), MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA returned p = 3.25e-07 (rank 1), and Mummichog m/z-network analysis returned p = 0.00798 (rank 4). The four driver metabolites driving this consensus are galactinol (alpha-D-galactosyl-(1→3)-1D-myo-inositol, KEGG:C01235), sucrose (KEGG:C00089), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), and glycerol (KEGG:C00116), all of which appear in the metabolites_hit rosters of both the RaMP and MetaboAnalystR results for KEGG:hsa00052 / KEGG:map00052. Galactinol is the most pathway-specific driver: it is the direct galactosyl donor to myo-inositol via galactitol intermediates within the Leloir pathway. A secondary cross-paradigm finding is Arachidonic Acid Metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism, p = 0.0236), driven by 8(S)-HPETE (KEGG:C14823), a 12-lipoxygenase product and the canonical substrate for specialized pro-resolving mediator biosynthesis. Glycerol appears as a shared metabolite in both the galactose and arachidonic-acid hits, acting as a backbone for glycerolipid/glycerophospholipid metabolism. Dopamine (KEGG:C03758) independently maps to tyrosine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00350, p = 0.1253) and GPCR downstream signalling (REACT:R-HSA-388396, FDR = 9.38e-06), consistent with its catecholamine biosynthesis route. D-Glucose (KEGG:C00221) participates in hexose phosphorylation and starch/sucrose metabolism without being a unique driver of any single high-significance pathway. The convergent signal across ORA (statistical over-representation) and m/z-network (empirical compound network) methods strongly implicates galactose/Leloir-pathway dysregulation as the primary metabolic consequence of the treatment.
